name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Antarctica)
why_used: Coldest, driest ice-free polar desert; permafrost and patterned ground like Mars mid/high latitudes; Phoenix-mission analog; drilling and life-detection tests.
notes: Ice-free area depends on the method: published estimates differ widely, and Levy 2012 (doi 10.1017/S0954102012000727) re-estimates it from Landsat. Radius 40 km ~ 4800 km2 equivalent. Point is the regional centre covering Taylor, Wright and Victoria valleys; the NASA page gives only 'roughly 77S, 161E', so the exact centre is an estimate.

name: Yungay / Atacama hyper-arid core (Chile)
why_used: Hyper-arid core with oxidant-rich soils (perchlorate); NASA life-detection drill and rover tests (ARADS 2015-2019, Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003).
notes: Point is Estacion Yungay (-24.083, -69.917). McKay et al. 2003 place the University of Antofagasta Desert Research Station near 24.08S, 69.99W (digits in the scan are garbled), about 6 km west; the 10 km radius covers both. The ARADS blind drill site (~22 km west, -24.102, -70.138) was not checked against a source. A person should confirm the point before this is marked verified.

name: Askja caldera and Dyngjufjoell (Iceland)
why_used: Fresh basalt with almost no vegetation; Apollo astronaut geology field training (1965 and 1967); basalt sedimentology and rover-mobility studies.
notes: Apollo astronauts trained at Askja caldera and Lake Myvatn (1965 and 1967). Evidence downgraded to secondary: no NASA page was found for the Iceland training. Askja caldera centre is 65.03N, 16.75W (Wikipedia gives 65.033N, 16.783W, about 1.5 km away). 20 km radius covers caldera and Dyngjufjoell.

name: HI-SEAS site on Mauna Loa (Hawaii)
why_used: Barren basalt slope at ~2500 m used for NASA-funded long-duration Mars-mission isolation simulations (Missions I-VI); lava tubes nearby.
notes: Habitat is located at 19.6022N, 155.4872W (matches Wikipedia). 10 km radius covers the surrounding sub-alpine basalt slope above the inversion layer. The NASA Goddard page supports the Mars-analog role; the NASA-funded Missions I-VI claim comes from University of Hawaii material, not that page.

name: Haughton impact crater (Devon Island Canada)
why_used: ~23 km impact crater in polar desert with permafrost and an impact-driven hydrothermal system; NASA Haughton-Mars Project field site since 1997.
notes: Apparent diameter ~23 km and final rim ~16 km; radius 12 km covers the apparent crater. The cited paper (Osinski et al. 2005) supports the crater geology. The Haughton-Mars Project since 1997 is described at https://marsinstitute.no/hmp; the nasa.gov project page returned 404.

name: Death Valley (USA)
why_used: Viking, MER, and MSL Mars analog; rover mobility, hazard detection, and sensor tests on rocky volcanic slopes (Mars Hill) and sand dunes.
notes: The NPS page names Mars Hill and the Mesquite Flat dunes as NASA test sites but gives no coordinates. Point is Mars Hill (-116.806, 36.364) with Mesquite Flat dunes ~38 km NW (-117.111, 36.606); neither coordinate has a checked source. A person should confirm before this is marked verified.

name: Puna de Atacama / Laguna Socompa (Argentina-Chile)
why_used: High-altitude (>3500 m) extreme UV evaporite lake with living stromatolites and microbialites; early-Mars lake analog.
notes: Coordinates pinpoint Laguna Socompa at base of Socompa Volcano (-24.536, -68.209), correcting the report's 67.2W typo. Studied by Farias et al. (2013).

name: Qaidam Basin western yardang and playa terrain (China)
why_used: Cold hyper-arid basin with yardangs, clay-sulfate weathering, and chloride playas; published Mars analog (Xiao et al. 2017, Sun et al. 2022).
notes: Centered on the western Qaidam yardang sampling transect (38.035N, 91.852E) and Dalangtan playa, correcting the report's eastern point.

name: Dallol and Danakil Depression (Ethiopia)
why_used: Acidic hypersaline hydrothermal field with iron-sulfate minerals; planetary field analog (Cavalazzi et al. 2019).
notes: Coordinates match Dallol crater and geothermal dome (14.242N, 40.300E). 15 km radius covers dome, Black Mountain, and salt canyons.

name: Craters of the Moon lava field (Idaho USA)
why_used: Young basaltic lava fields and lava tubes; Apollo astronaut geology training (1969) and NASA FINESSE research site.
notes: Lava field ~1500-1600 km2; radius 22 km ~ equivalent area. Wikipedia's monument centre (43.462N, 113.563W) is about 6 km from this point, inside the radius. Lunar and lava-tube relevance; keep out of Mars validation.

name: Harrat Khaybar and Umm Jirsan lava tube (Saudi Arabia)
why_used: Basaltic volcanic field with the 1.5 km Umm Jirsan lava tube; proposed subterranean lunar habitat analog (claim from the report only; Stewart et al. 2024 documents the cave and its archaeology).
notes: Coordinates match the paper's Umm Jirsan lava tube position (25.5888N, 39.7570E, WGS84). The paper is archaeology and does not mention the Moon or Mars as far as could be read; the planetary analog connection is the report's hypothesis.
